Prediction-Powered Category Proportion & Prevalence Estimation (PPI / PPI++)

Source: R/ppi_proportion.R
ppi_proportion.Rd

Estimates population class prevalences \(\pi_c = \mathbb{P}(Y = c)\) for binary or multi-class categorical content coding by combining a human-validated subset (truth_col observed) with a larger LLM-coded unlabeled corpus (pred_col only). Computes class-optimal PPI++ weights \(\hat{\lambda}_c^*\), the full joint \(K \times K\) asymptotic covariance matrix, marginal or family-wise simultaneous confidence intervals, and direct Human-Only and Naive-LLM benchmarks.

Usage

ppi_proportion(
  data,
  truth_col = "human_label",
  pred_col = "llm_label",
  unlabeled = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  lambda = "auto",
  conf_level = 0.95,
  simultaneous = FALSE,
  clamp_ci = TRUE,
  clip_lambda = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame (or llm_coded_data) containing truth_col and pred_col. When unlabeled = NULL, rows with non-missing truth_col form the labeled validation set and rows with is.na(truth_col) form the unlabeled set.

truth_col

Name of the human gold-standard categorical/binary column (factor, character, logical, or integer/numeric labels).

pred_col

Either a single column name of discrete LLM class labels (or binary predicted probabilities in [0, 1] when truth_col is binary 0/1 or logical), OR a named character vector mapping category levels to LLM predicted-probability column names (e.g., c(negative = "p_neg", neutral = "p_neu", positive = "p_pos")).

unlabeled

Optional separate data.frame of unlabeled observations.

levels

Optional character vector specifying the ordered category levels to estimate. If NULL, inferred from truth_col and pred_col.

lambda

Power-tuning parameter: "auto" (default: class-optimal PPI++), 1 (standard PPI), 0 (human-only), or a finite numeric scalar.

conf_level

Confidence level in (0, 1). Default 0.95.

simultaneous

Logical; if TRUE, computes family-wise simultaneous confidence intervals across all \(K\) categories using Bonferroni multiplicity control (\(\alpha / K\)). Default FALSE (marginal CIs).

clamp_ci

Logical; if TRUE (default), clamps confidence interval endpoints to [0, 1] while preserving exact unclipped standard errors.

clip_lambda

Logical; if TRUE, clips auto-tuned \(\hat{\lambda}_c^*\) to [0, 1]. Default FALSE.

Value

An S3 object of class c("llm_ppi_proportion", "llm_ppi") compatible with coef(), vcov(), confint(), print(), summary(), autoplot(), and format_apa_table().

Examples

set.seed(42)
n_tot <- 800
lvls <- c("low", "moderate", "high")
y_true <- factor(sample(lvls, n_tot, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.50, 0.30, 0.20)), levels = lvls)
# Biased LLM over-predicts "high" when true label is "moderate"
y_llm <- y_true
flip <- (y_true == "moderate") & (runif(n_tot) < 0.45)
y_llm[flip] <- "high"
df <- tibble::tibble(
  human_label = factor(
    c(as.character(y_true[1:150]), rep(NA_character_, n_tot - 150)),
    levels = lvls
  ),
  llm_label = y_llm
)
fit <- ppi_proportion(df, truth_col = "human_label", pred_col = "llm_label")
fit
#> 
#> ── Prediction-Powered Inference (ppi++) 
#> Labeled n = 150 | Unlabeled N = 650 | lambda = [0.81, 0.69, 0.49] | CI = 95%
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>   term     estimate std_error conf_low conf_high p_value var_gain
#>   <chr>       <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>      <dbl>
#> 1 low         0.524    0.0176    0.489     0.558 <0.0001     5.28
#> 2 moderate    0.307    0.031     0.247     0.368 <0.0001     1.59
#> 3 high        0.199    0.0271    0.146     0.252 <0.0001     1.63
